newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt signs satelite feeder link with U.S. WSI.
newsitem.headline: Egypt signs satelite feeder link with U.S. WSI.

text.p: U.S. telecommunication firm Worldcomm System Inc (WSI) signed a $1.38 million contract with Egypt to supply uplink equipment for the country's first satellite, an official said on Wednesday.
"The contract was signed on Tuesday," the official at the Egyptian Satellite Company/Nilesat, who declined to be named, told Reuters.

Nilesat earlier this year awarded Dutch firm Philips Electronics NV an $8.25 million contract to supply a digital broadcast system to be installed at Nilesat's control station in Cairo's satellite city in October.
Both the digital system and the feeder link will be operational by the end of September, the official said.
The satellite is expected to be launched by the end of November. A consortium led by French firm Matra Marconi Space in 1995 signed a $158 million contract to build and launch it.
In June last year, the state offered for sale to the public 20 percent of Nilesat at $100 per share.
The Egyptian Radio and Television Union (ERTU) holds a 40 percent stake in the firm and two public sector banks, National Bank of Egypt and Banque du Caire, own 7.5 percent each.
The Egyptian Company for Investment Projects has 15 percent of the satellite company and the state arms firm, Arab Organisation for Industrialisation, owns the final 10 percent.
The firm aims to make money by leasing satellite channels to television broadcasters.
